papers.title_in_file: Quantum Natural Gradient optimizer on noisy platforms: QAOA as a case study
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions and outlook, and the closing paragraphs of the superconducting-circuit results section; the method sections were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of the Quantum Natural Gradient optimizer against vanilla gradient descent for QAOA on the transverse field Ising model, on Rydberg-atom and superconducting-circuit platforms with noise.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in their simulations, QNG consistently outperformed Vanilla Gradient Descent, with faster convergence on average and greater robustness against random initializations of parameters.
quotes: Results demonstrate that QNG consistently outperforms Vanilla Gradient Descent, exhibiting faster convergence on average and greater robustness against random initializations of parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The conclusions qualify this: on the superconducting platform decoherence made ground state preparation unattainable, so the advantage is clearest on the Rydberg platform.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that, for QAOA on the transverse field Ising model with a realistic noise model from an IBM quantum device, QNG offers no advantage over Vanilla Gradient Descent, because both optimizers give unsatisfactory results.
quotes: Thus, we can conclude that for QAOA applied to the TFIM using quantum circuits with a realistic noise model from an IBM quantum device, QNG offers no advantage over Vanilla Gradient Descent, as both optimizers yield unsatisfactory results.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the primary objective is not to demonstrate state-of-the-art optimization performance, and that they adopt the TFIM as a toy model and testbed for benchmarking the behavior of QNG.
quotes: the primary objective of this work is not to demonstrate state-of-the-art optimization performance
we adopt the TFIM as a toy model, serving as a well-understood and controllable testbed for benchmarking the behavior of QNG
assertions.certainty_reason: Section I, p.2 states the study's own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that computing the full Quantum Fisher Information Matrix becomes impractical for a large number of parameters.
quotes: it is important to consider the cost associated with computing the full Quantum Fisher Information Matrix, which becomes impractical for a large number of parameters
assertions.certainty_reason: Section VII, p.14 is the paper's own statement of a limit.

papers.title_in_file: Uncovering Quantum Many-body Scars with Quantum Machine Learning
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, results summary, hardware validation passage and discussion; the model-specific derivations were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation and IBM-hardware study that uses enhanced quantum convolutional neural networks to identify known and new non-thermal eigenstates in chaotic many-body spin models.

assertions.value: The authors report that, in simulations, their QCNNs achieve over 99% single-shot measurement accuracy in identifying all known scars.
quotes: Our simulations demonstrate that QCNNs achieve over 99% single-shot measurement accuracy in identifying all known scars.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors report single-shot measurement accuracy exceeding 63% on IBM quantum devices under real-world noise and errors, with the aid of error mitigation techniques.
quotes: achieving single-shot measurement accuracy exceeding 63% under real-world noise and errors, with the aid of error mitigation techniques
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical hardware result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The hardware accuracy is far below the simulated one, so noise costs a large share of the signal.

assertions.value: The authors state that preparing eigenstates of many-body systems remains a computationally challenging task, and that scaling up system sizes will still rely on quantum hardware.
quotes: Preparing eigenstates of many-body systems remains a computationally challenging task.
Scaling up system sizes will still rely on quantum hardware
assertions.certainty_reason: Section III, p.9 is the paper's own statement of a limit.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Machine Learning on Near-Term Quantum Devices: Current State of Supervised and Unsupervised Techniques for Real-World Applications
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, the barren plateau and optimizer passages, a sample of the application sections, and the discussion of open problems; the many application summaries were not all read.
papers.what_it_is: A survey of supervised and unsupervised QML applications run on real quantum hardware, covering encoding, ansatz, error mitigation and gradient methods.

assertions.value: The authors state that the survey focuses on selected supervised and unsupervised learning applications executed on quantum hardware, tailored for real-world scenarios.
quotes: This survey focuses on selected supervised and unsupervised learning applications executed on quantum hardware, specifically tailored for real-world scenarios.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1 states the survey's own scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that quantum reinforcement learning is not addressed in the survey and refer readers to other overviews.
quotes: Although not addressed in our current survey, we direct readers to
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 1, p.1 states what the survey leaves out.

assertions.value: The authors state that many QML studies that show promising results on benchmark datasets often fail to provide open-source reference implementations, which hinders reproducibility and raises concern about positive bias.
quotes: Many studies that demonstrate promising results on benchmark datasets often fail to provide open-source reference implementations of their competitive algorithms.
raises concerns about potential positive bias
assertions.certainty_reason: The survey's own observation, not backed by a counted sample in the passage read.
assertions.reader_inference: Relevant to how much weight a published QML benchmark result should carry.

papers.what_it_is: A short theory paper that proposes a variational quantum eigensolver variant which samples the circuits once and does the energy minimization on a classical processor.

assertions.value: The authors present a cascaded VQE algorithm that needs to run a set of quantum circuits once, not at every iteration of parameter optimization, which they say increases computational throughput.
quotes: that only requires the execution of a set of quantum circuits once rather than at every iteration during the parameter optimization process, thereby increasing the computational throughput
assertions.certainty_reason: A design claim with an analytic count, no hardware or numeric benchmark in the text read.
assertions.reader_inference: No quantum-hardware run is reported in the text read, so the throughput gain rests on the circuit-count argument.

assertions.value: The authors state that the algorithm uses a quantum processing unit to probe the needed probability mass functions and a classical processing unit to perform the remaining calculations, including the energy minimization.
quotes: This algorithm uses a quantum processing unit to probe the needed probability mass functions and a classical processing unit perform the remaining calculations, including the energy minimization.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1 states the method's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that one downside of the VQE algorithm is that computational throughput is limited by the large number of quantum circuit executions needed on the quantum processing unit.
quotes: One downside of the VQE algorithm is that the computational throughput is limited by the large number of needed quantum circuit executions on the quantum processing unit (QPU).
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' characterization of a baseline method, without evidence in the paper.

papers.title_in_file: Tensor-network-based variational Monte Carlo approach to the non-equilibrium steady state of open quantum systems
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, conclusions and perspectives, and the end of the results section; the method derivation was skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A classical algorithm that finds the steady state of open many-body quantum spin systems by variational Monte Carlo over a matrix product operator.

assertions.value: The authors state that their approach outperforms and offers several advantages over comparable algorithms, such as improved scaling of the computational cost with respect to the bond dimension for periodic systems.
quotes: Our approach outperforms and offers several advantages over comparable algorithms, such as an improved scaling of the computational cost with respect to the bond dimension for periodic systems.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim in the abstract.
assertions.reader_inference: This is a classical simulation method. It bears on QC only as a classical baseline for simulating open quantum systems.

assertions.value: The authors state that they demonstrate the method on the dissipative quantum Ising model with collective dephasing and long-ranged power law interactions, for spin chains of up to N = 100 spins.
quotes: We showcase the versatility of our approach by studying the phase diagrams and correlation functions of the dissipative quantum Ising model with collective dephasing and long-ranged power law interactions for spin chains of up to N = 100 spins.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1 states the study's own setup and scope.

assertions.value: The authors state that the main bottleneck preventing effective simulation of larger systems is the computation of the log-derivatives of the Lindbladian, whose cost grows with the square of the system size.
quotes: The main bottleneck preventing effective simulation of larger systems is the computation of the logderivatives of the Lindbladian in Eq. (13), the cost of which scales as N 2 with the system size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 5, p.9 is the paper's own statement of a limit.

papers.title_in_file: Multi-Agent Quantum Reinforcement Learning using Evolutionary Optimization
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, the discussion passage before the conclusion, and the conclusion; the method and experiment details were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A simulation study of gradient-free, evolutionary training of variational quantum circuits for multi-agent reinforcement learning in the Coin Game.

assertions.value: The authors report that their VQC approaches performed significantly better than a neural network with a similar number of trainable parameters, and achieved similar results to a larger neural network using 97.88% fewer parameters.
quotes: We showed that our Variational Quantum Circuit approaches perform significantly better compared to a neural network with a similar amount of trainable parameters. Compared to the larger neural network, our approaches archive similar results using 97.88% less parameters.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study in one small environment.
assertions.reader_inference: The comparison is against evolutionary-trained neural networks, not gradient-trained ones, as the authors note in their future work.

assertions.value: The authors state that they evaluate their genetic variations in the Coin Game environment and also compare them to classical approaches.
quotes: We evaluate our genetic variations in the Coin Game environment and also compare them to classical approaches.
assertions.certainty_reason: Abstract, p.1 states the study's own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that barren plateaus did not arise for their gradient-free approach in the experiments, but that it cannot be ruled out that such issues may occur in gradient-free methods under different conditions or in more complex scenarios.
quotes: For our gradient-free approach used in the experiments, barren plateaus did not arise; however, it cannot be ruled out that such issues may occur in gradient-free methods under different conditions or in more complex scenarios
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7 is the paper's own statement of a limit.

assertions.value: The authors state that the VQC results could in future be run on real quantum hardware, not only on a quantum simulator, to determine whether there is a difference.
quotes: the VQC results could be run not only on a quantum simulator, but on real quantum hardware to determine which and if there is a difference
assertions.certainty_reason: Section 7 is the paper's own statement of what it did not do.
assertions.reader_inference: The results come from a quantum simulator, not hardware.

papers.title_in_file: Implementing transferable annealing protocols for combinatorial optimisation on neutral atom quantum processors: a case study on smart-charging of electric vehicles
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, the end of the results, and the conclusion and outlook; the method and appendices were skimmed.
papers.what_it_is: A Pasqal and EDF study of transferable Bayesian-optimized annealing schedules for Maximum Independent Set on a neutral-atom processor, applied to an electric-vehicle smart-charging problem.

assertions.value: The authors report that for Maximum Independent Set problems on graph families with shared geometries, optimal parameters concentrate, which enables efficient transfer between similar instances and from smaller to larger ones.
quotes: Our study reveals that, for Maximum Independent Set problems on graph families with shared geometries, optimal parameters naturally concentrate, enabling efficient transferability between similar instances and from smaller to larger ones.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The authors work for Pasqal, which makes the platform, so this is partly a vendor description of its own hardware.

assertions.value: The authors report that experimental results on the Orion Alpha platform validate the approach, scaling to problems with up to 100 qubits.
quotes: Experimental results on the Orion Alpha platform validate the effectiveness of our approach, scaling to problems with up to 100 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors from the platform vendor describe results on the vendor's own platform.
assertions.reader_inference: Orion Alpha is a Pasqal platform, so the validation is not independent.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method relies on all dataset graphs being subgraphs of a shared atomic layout, which limits encoding of larger industrial instances that involve more constraints than the layout can accommodate.
quotes: The method leverages the fact that all graphs in the dataset are subgraphs of a shared atomic layout. However, this dependence poses a limitation for encoding larger industrial instances, which often involve significantly more constraints than the atomic layout can accommodate.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Conclusion and Outlook section is the paper's own statement of a limit.

papers.title_in_file: Variational Quantum Monte Carlo investigations of the superconducting pairing in La3Ni2O7
papers.partial_detail: Abstract, introduction, summary and the start of the method appendix.
papers.what_it_is: A classical condensed-matter study that uses variational quantum Monte Carlo (a classical numerical method) on Hubbard and t-J models of the nickelate superconductor La3Ni2O7.
papers.why_not: The paper uses variational quantum Monte Carlo as a classical numerical method for superconducting pairing in a material. It involves no quantum computer, no machine learning workload and no finance or evaluation-method content.
